verdict.summary: Strava's API Policy effective June 1, 2026 bans using Strava data 'in connection with the development, training, evaluation, or operation of any AI Application', explicitly including ingestion into a context window, RAG and grounding, so a third-party AI agent can't legitimately read Strava data via OAuth; Strava points users to its own Strava MCP instead. For non-AI apps, setup is self-serve but needs a Strava subscription, starts at 1 athlete (10 after a self-serve upgrade), and needs a discretionary Developer Program review with no SLA beyond that.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the app at strava.com/settings/api (needs a Strava subscription), set the callback domain to localhost, and authorize your own account. Single Player Mode only lets you access your own data.

timeToProd.assumes: An AI agent reading users' activities, which the 2026 API Policy prohibits; the hours shown are our estimate for a non-AI app going through Developer Program review to exceed 10 athletes.
timeToProd.waitingOn: For AI use: nothing will unlock it under current terms. For non-AI apps: Developer Program admission, which Strava says is discretionary with 'no fixed review-time service-level agreement'.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The AI prohibition and lack of SLA are sourced; the non-AI timing is our estimate.

verdict.cost: A Strava subscription is required to create an app; Standard Tier apps may also require the developer or specified end users to keep an active subscription.

prerequisites.item: A Strava account with an active subscription
prerequisites.why: Strava says 'A Strava subscription is a prerequisite for creating an app', and Standard Tier apps are subject to subscription requirements.

prerequisites.item: A use case that doesn't involve any AI Application
prerequisites.why: Section 5.3 of the API Policy prohibits training, grounding, embeddings, RAG and ingestion into a context window or working memory with Strava data.

prerequisites.item: Compliance with brand guidelines and a 'Connect with Strava' button
prerequisites.why: Developer Program submissions need screenshots of every place Strava data appears and of the connect button.

prerequisites.item: A callback domain for your redirect URIs
prerequisites.why: redirect_uri must be within the registered callback domain; localhost and 127.0.0.1 are allowed.

scopeTiers.impact: New apps start at athlete capacity 1 (your own data); a self-serve upgrade in API settings raises it to 10 with 200 read / 400 overall requests per 15 min.
Same capacity limits. activity:read_all adds Only You activities and privacy zone data; scopes don't change the review path, the athlete count does.

steps.title: Check the use case against the API Policy
steps.detail: Read Section 5.3 (no AI Applications, including context-window ingestion), 5.4 (no analytics or combining with other data), 5.5 (no persistent indexes or vector stores) and 6.2 (7-day cache). If your product is an AI agent, stop here.

steps.title: Get a Strava subscription
steps.detail: Sign up at strava.com and subscribe; a subscription is required to create an app.

steps.title: Create the API application
steps.detail: Go to My API Application, enter name, website and Authorization Callback Domain (localhost while building), and copy the client ID and secret.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: strava.com/settings/api returned 301 to /login on 2026-10-20. We did not sign in.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize (or /oauth/mobile/authorize) with comma-separated scopes; exchange and refresh at https://www.strava.com/oauth/token; always store the newest refresh token.

steps.title: Use webhooks instead of polling
steps.detail: Subscribe to webhook events and throttle backfills using rate-limit response headers; Strava says apps under 100 users hitting limits usually poll inefficiently.

steps.title: Upgrade to 10 athletes
steps.detail: From the API Settings dashboard, upgrade access: capacity 1 to 10, read limit 200/15 min and 2,000/day, overall 400/15 min and 4,000/day.

steps.title: Implement deletion and revocation
steps.detail: Delete user data on request or disconnect (with written confirmation), expire caches after 7 days, and use POST /oauth/revoke (the legacy /oauth/deauthorize goes away on June 1, 2027).

steps.title: Prepare Developer Program screenshots
steps.detail: Capture every screen showing Strava data and the 'Connect with Strava' button, following brand guidelines.

steps.title: Submit the Developer Program form
steps.detail: Submit once you're near 10 connected athletes.

steps.title: Wait for Strava's decision
steps.detail: Admission is discretionary with no fixed review-time SLA; you hear back only if admitted or if Strava needs more information.

agentCanDo: Review the use case against API Policy sections 5.3–5.5 and 6.2
Implement OAuth with refresh token rotation and /oauth/revoke
Build webhook ingestion and header-based throttling
Implement 7-day cache expiry and user data deletion

blockers.symptom: Your product is an AI agent or LLM app that would read users' activities
blockers.cause: API Policy 5.3 prohibits using Strava data with any AI Application, including ingestion into a context window or working memory, grounding and RAG.
blockers.fix: No OAuth fix; Strava directs subscribers to its own Strava MCP for personal AI use, which isn't authorized for commercial or third-party access.

blockers.symptom: A second athlete can't authorize your app
blockers.cause: New apps start in Single Player Mode with athlete capacity 1.
blockers.fix: Use the self-serve upgrade to 10; beyond that, submit for Developer Program review.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 after a backfill or polling loop
blockers.cause: Default limits: 200 overall / 100 read requests per 15 min and 2,000 / 1,000 per day, per application.
blockers.fix: Use webhooks, throttle on rate-limit headers, and upgrade to the 10-athlete limits.

blockers.cause: Missing or wrong client_id in the token request.
blockers.fix: Send client_id, client_secret, code and grant_type to /oauth/token.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token with only grant_type returned this 400 body on 2026-10-20.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails with an old refresh token
blockers.cause: When a new refresh token is issued, the old one is invalidated immediately.
blockers.fix: Persist the newest refresh token from every token response.

blockers.symptom: Can't create an app in API settings
blockers.cause: A Strava subscription is a prerequisite for creating an app.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 6 hours; refreshing with more than an hour left returns the same token.
Strava data from a user may be shown only to that user, never to other users, even if it's public on Strava.
Cached Strava data may be kept for at most 7 days, and storage in vector stores, embedding stores or search indexes is prohibited.
You may not charge end users for access to Strava API functionality or resell access, and you may not combine Strava data with other customer data for analytics.
The API Agreement says API access is currently free but Strava may introduce pricing, including differentiated pricing for business users.
Strava may restrict or remove endpoints and keeps an allowlist for apps allowed to keep using deprecated ones.
